channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Janja intervém em estresse na elaboração do programa de governo de Lula
item.description: First Lady Janja intervened to resolve a stress-inducing issue in the drafting of Lula's government program, set to be unveiled in August. The situation caused internal tension within the campaign team, requiring her mediation to maintain cohesion in the plan. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: PL aciona TSE contra páginas fantasmas e cita quase R$ 3 milhões gastos em ataques a Flávio
item.description: The PL party has filed a complaint with the TSE against an alleged digital militia operating through 'phantom' profiles designed to attack its members, particularly Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The party claims nearly R$ 3 million was spent on disinformation campaigns and coordinated attacks against him, aiming to damage his reputation and electoral prospects. The PL is demanding an investigation and accountability for these actions.

item.title: Renan Santos prega ruptura com Lula, mas livro do Missão ecoa propostas do adversário e da esquerda
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for President, positions himself as a defender of freedoms and a critic of the Lula government, but his party, Missão, presents in the 'Yellow Book' proposals that align with left-wing agendas, such as media regulation, de-dollarization, and greater prominence for emerging nations. The party states that the published fascicles are not definitive, but essayistic texts with a manifesto character, and does not comment on the ideas of media regulation and economic de-dollarization. The 'Yellow Book' is a six-volume collection intended to guide the party's political project, claiming to go beyond left and 'centrão' narratives.

item.title: Tarifaço: governo Lula crê que EUA só retomará conversas após eleição
item.description: The Lula government believes the United States will only resume trade negotiations with Brazil, including the 25% tariff on Brazilian products, after the 2026 presidential election. This assessment is based on the view that the Trump administration sees little advantage in negotiating with a government that does not meet its desired concessions, particularly regarding restrictions on Chinese investments in critical minerals and rare earths, a proposal Brazil rejected. Although the tariff is set to take effect on July 22, the Executive seeks to expand the list of exceptions but sees no U.S. willingness to advance dialogue in the short term.

item.title: Senado tem semestre marcado por cabo de guerra entre Alcolumbre e Lula
item.description: The Senate semester was defined by intense clashes between Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and the Lula government, culminating in the historic rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF. Alcolumbre orchestrated votes against the administration, including overturning the dosimetry veto, and moved closer to the opposition, particularly Flávio Bolsonaro. Despite 258 matters deliberated and 206 approved, institutional relations were severely strained.

item.title: O clã Bolsonaro não aguenta dez minutos de perguntas de verdade hoje
item.description: The Blog do Noblat program highlighted the weakening of Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy, citing a 60-day delay in financial reporting for the controversial film Dark Horse, linked to Daniel Vorcaro, and the lack of answers regarding his ties to militias and rumored compromising videos. Ricardo Noblat and Bob Fernandes criticized the absence of incisive journalism in current political coverage, contrasting it with the courage of reporters like Soninha Carneiro. The Bolsonaro clan is described as unable to withstand tough questioning today.

item.title: Ciranda política
item.description: Regardless of who wins the 2026 election, Brazil will remain hostage to an outdated political class until at least 2030, with little renewal expected—similar to the stagnation since 1994. The article draws a parallel to Fernando Henrique Cardoso’s emergence via the PSDB, which broke from the worn-out MDB and represented a modern political vision at the time.

item.title: Quem será o vice de Flávio? Para onde vão PP e União? As principais perguntas às vésperas das convenções partidárias
item.description: Party conventions until August 5 will define strategic alliances for the 2026 elections. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) still lacks a running mate, seeks to attract Republicans and PP-União, but faces the risk of neutrality from these parties, which would isolate his ticket. In Rio, the PP-União federation tends toward neutrality, harming PL and benefiting Eduardo Paes, while Michelle Bolsonaro’s Senate candidacy in the DF is in jeopardy after criticizing her stepson.

item.title: Fragmentação de candidaturas na direita ameaça plano bolsonarista de eleger maioria no Senado
item.description: The fragmentation of right-wing candidacies in at least six states — including Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais and São Paulo — threatens Bolsonaro’s goal of securing a Senate majority to advance agendas such as the impeachment of Supreme Court justices. The insistence of pre-candidates to remain in the race risks splitting the right-wing vote, opening space for opponents and undermining efforts to build a governing coalition in Congress.

item.title: Campanha de Tarcísio planeja desgaste de Haddad por atuação em Itaipu
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' re-election campaign plans to attack Fernando Haddad over his role as a board member of Itaipu Binacional from 2023 to 2026, citing lack of transparency and undisclosed compensation, despite the ongoing tariff impasse at the dam. The strategy also highlights infrastructure deliveries such as the Rodoanel and Line 6-Orange of the metro, while aiming to reduce opponents through the withdrawal of Paulo Serra and Kim Kataguiri to boost first-round victory prospects.

item.title: O mais importante sobre o novo tarifaço não é a tarifa
item.description: The new U.S. tariffs against Brazil should not be reduced to just another chapter in the Trump-Lula relationship, but rather seen as a sign of a deeper structural shift in global trade relations. Overemphasizing the personal dimension of leaders obscures the fact that these tariffs reflect a new protectionist logic that could redefine Brazilian exporters' access to the U.S. market, regardless of who is in power. Focusing on personalities distracts from the need for a long-term Brazilian strategy to navigate increasingly selective trade blocs.

item.title: ‘Só de saber que ele acredita no meu sonho, eu acredito ainda mais’, diz surfista sobre bastidores de patrocínio firmado com Matheus Cunha
item.description: Brazil national team forward Matheus Cunha has decided to sponsor professional surfer Israel Júnior, who competes in the WSL Qualifying Series, after connecting through mutual friends and driven by his genuine passion for surfing, nurtured in Baía Formosa (RN). The sponsorship will cover travel, accommodation, and entry fees for international events, helping Israel maintain his regional ranking and pursue a spot in the Challenger Series.

item.title: Kassab nega influenciar destino de emendas como presidente do PSD
item.description: PSD president Gilberto Kassab denied before the STF having influenced the allocation of parliamentary amendments during his tenure, responding to an order by Minister Flávio Dino after statements by Valdemar Costa Neto (PL), who admitted interfering in the process. Kassab stated the PSD never mentioned influencing amendment allocation and that his presidency did not participate in deliberations on distribution criteria. Dino had previously frozen R$ 119 million in Costa Neto’s accounts and suspended amendments due to evidence of an irregular scheme involving Chamber staff, suggesting possible embezzlement.

item.title: Boné de Trump pode custar caro a Tarcísio
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas, the São Paulo gubernatorial candidate with a 16-point lead over Fernando Haddad, faces his first setback after appearing in a January 2025 video wearing a Donald Trump campaign cap with the MAGA slogan. He has until October to explain the incident, which could cause political damage amid international polarization and electoral sensitivity.

item.title: Trump pode interferir na eleição para favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro e gerar caos, diz brasilianista
item.description: Brazilianist Anthony W. Pereira warns that Donald Trump could interfere in Brazil's 2026 elections to favor Flávio Bolsonaro, risking democratic chaos. He argues that authoritarianism is a shared threat to the political systems of both the U.S. and Brazil, and his visit aims to analyze these crises at a Cebrap event.

item.title: Gleisi rebate crítica de Flávio Bolsonaro à Maria da Penha: "Ignorante"
item.description: Deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) harshly criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for calling the Maria da Penha Law a "piece of paper", labeling him ignorant and defending the law's effectiveness in combating domestic violence. Flávio Bolsonaro reiterated during a political event in Espírito Santo that his potential government would adopt more effective measures to protect women, including harsher penalties for aggressors, while dismissing the current law as insufficient.

item.title: Morre Matheus Azevedo, irmão mais novo do senador Cleitinho
item.description: Matheus Azevedo, the younger brother of Senator Cleitinho (Republicanos-MG), died on July 18, 2026, in Divinópolis (MG) after battling leukemia. His death was confirmed by state deputy Eduardo Azevedo (PL-MG), prompting condolences from politicians including Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), Romeu Zema (Novo-MG), and André Janones (Rede-MG), who expressed solidarity with the family. The funeral was held on July 19, and the city declared three days of official mourning.

item.title: Senadora Soraya Thronicke posta foto com Lula e confirma pré-candidatura à reeleição
item.description: Senator Soraya Thronicke (PSB-MS) confirmed yesterday, the 17th, that she will run for re-election to the Senate in 2026. She posted a photo alongside President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) on her social media, accompanied by the statement: 'Am I a pre-candidate for re-election? I never stopped being one!'.

item.title: “Não há nenhuma possibilidade”, diz Michelle sobre ser vice de Zema
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro denied any possibility of being Romeu Zema’s running mate in the 2026 election, stating she has not yet decided on her candidacy and that, as a PL member, she cannot run for a majoritarian office. Zema said at a Novo event that Michelle is one of the options for vice-president, provided she has a clean record, and that the decision will be made by August 5. Michelle said her current priority is caring for Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.

item.title: "Nenhuma possibilidade", diz Michelle Bolsonaro sobre ser vice de Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) mentioned Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) as a potential vice-presidential candidate for his 2026 ticket, but she rejected the idea, stating there is "no possibility" of accepting, as she has not yet decided whether to run for Senate and her party, the PL, already has Flávio Bolsonaro as a presidential pre-candidate, which would prevent two tickets from the same party running in different coalitions for major offices. Michelle also said she is currently prioritizing care for her husband, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Zema diz que Michelle Bolsonaro é sua opção para vice, mas ela nega
item.description: Romeu Zema, a pre-candidate for president from the Novo party, mentioned Michelle Bolsonaro as a potential vice-presidential running mate for 2026, praising her clean record. Shortly after, Michelle denied the possibility, stating she has not yet decided on a candidacy and that, as a PL member, she cannot be on a ticket with another PL candidate for different offices.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: a candidatura de um homem só
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy initially gained momentum by capitalizing on Lula's unpopularity and government inertia, but quickly deteriorated due to scandals involving a request for 134 million reais from a banker linked to Brazil's largest banking fraud, Michelle Bolsonaro's public denunciation of humiliation, and backlash from Trump-era tariffs that undermined the family's nationalist image. After leading in April, he now trails Lula by eight points in July according to Genial/Quaest poll.

item.title: Como Michelle trabalhou pela prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, que por pouco não foi revogada
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro worked behind the scenes to secure house arrest for Jair Bolsonaro, leveraging contacts with STF ministers such as Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes through private meetings, medical documentation, and a conciliatory tone. Although her efforts were nearly reversed, she succeeded in maintaining the measure, which nonetheless caused discomfort among hardline bolsonaristas due to her cooperative demeanor and remarks like 'brother in Christ'.

item.title: Quem é o ex-Bope que vai concorrer ao governo do Rio
item.description: Colonel João Jacques Busnello, former subcommander of Rio de Janeiro’s Military Police Special Operations Battalion (Bope), has been announced as the pre-candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro by the Missão party. He gained notoriety in 2009 as a sniper who killed a hostage-taker in Vila Isabel and ran unsuccessfully for federal deputy in 2018 and 2022. The Missão party, linked to the MBL, has Renan Santos as its pre-candidate for president.

item.title: A motivação política de Trump pró Bolsonaro não é uma hipótese, é um fato
item.description: The tariff crisis between Brazil and the U.S. is politically motivated by Trump, who imposed 50% tariffs to pressure Brazil into dropping the case against Jair Bolsonaro for attempted coup, as evidenced by a July 2025 letter. Despite Brazil’s technical efforts and private sector engagement, the U.S. refused dialogue, creating unilateral obstacles based on false claims about Pix, deforestation, and trade. Brazil’s response must be measured: avoid pure retaliation but also not passively accept attacks threatening jobs and strategic sectors.

item.title: Missão lança ex-sniper do Bope como pré-candidato ao governo do Rio
item.description: The Mission party announced the pre-candidacy of Military Police Colonel and former BOPE sniper, Coronel Busnello, for the Rio de Janeiro governorship. The name was revealed during the congress of the Free Brazil Movement (MBL) by the party's presidential pre-candidate, Renan Santos. This replaces the initially selected military firefighter Rafa Luz, who had been chosen to lead the ticket.

item.title: Novo adia definição de vice de Zema
item.description: The Novo party postponed the decision on the vice-presidential candidate for Romeu Zema's presidential ticket until after the party's national convention, scheduled for July 27 in Brasília. The announcement was made by national party president Eduardo Ribeiro during the National Meeting of the party in São Paulo on Saturday, the 18th.

item.title: Renan Santos anuncia chapa do Missão ao governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for President, announced the Missão party's ticket for the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial race, naming Colonel Busnello as the gubernatorial candidate and military firefighter Rafa Luz as his running mate. Santos emphasized the need to combat crime and corruption in the state, pledging federal support and possible intervention if elected president. The event took place at a sports club in Rio's South Zone.

item.title: Assim como Michelle, Girão critica apoio da direita a Ciro no Ceará
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) criticized right-wing support for Ciro Gomes' (PSDB) gubernatorial candidacy in Ceará, arguing it would strengthen a potential presidential bid by Ciro in 2030. He accused conservative parties of backing a 'hard-left' representative, aligning with Michelle Bolsonaro's opposition to a PL-Ciro alliance in the state.

item.title: Flávio chama Lei Maria da Penha de “pedaço de papel”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) denounced the Maria da Penha Law as 'a piece of paper' at a PL event in Vitória, advocating harsher penalties for domestic violence offenders and praising former mayor Lorenzo Pazolini's policies as a model. He also unveiled the 'Brazil for Her' program, pledging free internet for 70 million women without specifying funding sources.

item.title: Celina e Damares apostam que Michelle estará com Flávio Bolsonaro no palanque
item.description: District Governor Celina Leão (PP) and Senator Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF), close allies of Michelle Bolsonaro, believe the rift between her and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro will be overcome and are actively working to reconcile the family. They urged Michelle to remain in the PL after she stepped down from leading PL Mulher, and now affirm she will run for Senate while Flávio Bolsonaro is their presidential candidate, with the party’s full support on the campaign trail. Celina emphasized Michelle’s crucial influence over evangelical women voters to prevent a repeat of the 2022 defeat.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa diz ao Democracia Cristã que não será candidato à Presidência
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa informed the Christian Democracy party that he will not run for president in 2026, citing lack of resources and party structure. His withdrawal follows poor polling performance, with just 1% voter intention in the latest Genial/Quaest survey. Barbosa had been announced as a pre-candidate in May, triggering an internal party crisis that previously backed Aldo Rebelo as the presidential hopeful.

item.title: Missão anuncia Coronel Busnello como candidato ao governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The Mission party announced Coronel Busnello, former BOPE sniper, as its candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, reversing a previous ticket that had military firefighter Rafa Luz as the gubernatorial candidate. Luz will now run as vice-governor. The announcement was made at the MBL Congress by Renan Santos, Mission’s presidential pre-candidate, who praised Busnello as a battle hero and stated that public security will be the central theme of the campaign.

item.title: Lula passa a mão na cabeça de ladrão de celular, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of defending cellphone thieves, claiming Lula 'pats the head' of thieves, in criticism of the Celular Seguro program. Lula had stated that people with stolen cellphones should not fear going to police stations to return them, without risk of arrest. Bolsonaro's claim contrasts with Article 180 of the Penal Code, which criminalizes receiving stolen goods, even without intent, with penalties of detention or fines.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro copia Barroso e lança IA com mesmo nome de ferramenta inaugurada pelo STF
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro launched an AI tool named MarIA, sharing the same name as the one used by the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) since December 2024, targeting women with features like mammogram scheduling, protective measure monitoring, and psychological support. While the naming coincidence surprised judges, the STF did not trademark the name as it was deemed institutional, meaning no legal irregularity occurred in the campaign's use.

item.title: “Aldo é opção zero”
item.description: Following Joaquim Barbosa's withdrawal from the presidential race for the Christian Democracy (DC) party, the party ruled out reviving Aldo Rebelo's pre-candidacy, stating he is not a viable alternative. Party president João Caldas described Aldo as 'option zero,' indicating his candidacy will not be considered to replace Barbosa.

item.title: Haddad diz que gestão Tarcísio faz São Paulo 'andar para trás' e critica segurança, educação e economia
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) of São Paulo, stating the state is 'going backwards' in education, sanitation, public safety, and the economy. He noted São Paulo's 2023 growth was only 0.5%, compared to Brazil's 2.3%, and accused the governor of exaggerating achievements, such as reducing homelessness, which actually rose by 186%. Haddad also claimed Tarcísio prioritizes propaganda over effective public policies.

item.title: A pista de que Alexandre de Moraes vai endurecer para cima do TSE
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes is closely monitoring the Electoral Justice's actions in the 2026 elections, ordering the Electoral Public Ministry to investigate whether Flávio Bolsonaro committed premature campaigning by reading a letter from Jair Bolsonaro endorsing him as a presidential pre-candidate. Although the letter does not explicitly ask for votes, Moraes views it as a potential electoral offense, as it promotes Flávio as Brazil's savior. Known for his hardline stance against disinformation and bolsonarism, Moraes aims to centralize electoral investigations involving malicious speech at the TSE, countering the perceived leniency of the current Electoral Court.

item.title: Zema diz que Michelle é opção para vice em sua chapa
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), pre-candidate for president in 2026, stated that Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) is one of the options for vice-president on his ticket, emphasizing the importance of being 'clean slate'. He clarified that no decision has been made and that the choice will be finalized by August 5, 2026, the deadline for party conventions. Novo’s national president, Eduardo Ribeiro, confirmed talks with Podemos about a possible alliance, but no decision has been reached.

item.title: Flávio diz que Moraes “parece um demônio” após restrições a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president in 2026, said he will grant amnesty to those involved in the January 8, 2023 attacks if elected. Speaking at a PL event in Espírito Santo, he also criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, calling him 'like a demon' following restrictions imposed on Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: 33% do eleitorado brasileiro vê culpa de Lula e Bolsonaro em aumento das bets, diz pesquisa
item.description: A More in Common/Ipsos-Ipos poll finds that 33% of Brazilian voters blame both Lula’s and Bolsonaro’s governments for the rise of betting platforms, while 35% say neither administration is responsible. The results indicate a split perception regarding the origins of the online gambling market’s expansion in Brazil.

item.title: Zema volta a prometer privatizar Petrobras e BB e classificar facções criminosas como terroristas
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's pre-candidate for president, pledged to privatize Petrobras and Banco do Brasil to fund infrastructure, classified criminal factions as terrorists, and proposed a minimum 25-year sentence for their members. He also criticized STF ministers Alexandre de Moraes and Gilmar Mendes, advocating for their impeachment and claiming no other right-wing candidate challenges the 'untouchables' as fiercely as he does.

item.title: O slogan que o partido Novo vai adotar na campanha
item.description: The Novo party unveiled its new national slogan: 'Together we will build a country made for us'. The announcement was made at the opening of the party’s national meeting in São Paulo, where a video emphasized members’ private-sector backgrounds and criticized figures such as President Lula, Minister Alexandre de Moraes, and banker Daniel Vorcaro as 'untouchables'.

item.title: ”Não vou baixar a cabeça para tirano”, diz Flávio sobre Moraes
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes for restricting visits to former President Jair Bolsonaro, accusing him of acting like a 'tyrant' and overstepping his authority by interfering in matters that should fall under the TSE. The restriction followed Flávio's Instagram post of a letter from his father requesting votes and naming him as his 'spokesperson' in the 2026 presidential race, which violated the terms of house arrest. Flávio declared he would not 'bow down to any tyrant' and noted that Jair Bolsonaro's defense claimed they were unaware of the letter's prior publication.

item.title: Após decisão sobre prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, Flávio chama Moraes de 'sem alma' em evento do PL no ES
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro harshly criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, calling him 'soulless' and comparing him to a 'demon using a person to do harm,' during a PL event in Espírito Santo. The remarks followed Moraes’ decision to maintain Jair Bolsonaro’s house arrest and restrict visits with political-electoral purposes until the end of the 2026 elections. Flávio also advocated for strengthening the right-wing bloc in Congress and expressed hope of reuniting with his father soon.

item.title: Maria da Penha é "pedaço de papel" que não defende mulher, diz Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the Maria da Penha Law, calling it a "piece of paper" that does not defend women, and asserted that women's protection is a right-wing agenda. He announced the "Brazil for Them" program and proposals such as distributing cell phones to low-income women, while praising Lorenzo Pazolini's actions as mayor of Vitória.

item.title: Zema promete privatizar Petrobras e Banco do Brasil e usar recursos em obras de infraestrutura
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo Party's pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidency, pledged to privatize Petrobras and Banco do Brasil to fund nationwide infrastructure projects such as highways, railways, and ports. He criticized President Lula, affirmative action policies, and progressive education, while advocating to label criminal factions as terrorist organizations with minimum 25-year sentences. Zema also stated he aims to build a Senate majority to impeach Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Novo confirmará candidatura de Zema na convenção, mas deve adiar definição sobre vice
item.description: The Novo Party will confirm Romeu Zema’s presidential candidacy at its national convention on July 27 but postpone the decision on his running mate, delegating it to the National Executive Committee. The strategy aims to keep alliance options open with neutral parties or those supporting Flávio Bolsonaro, hoping for potential damage to the Bolsonaro candidate before the August 15 TSE registration deadline. The party is also in talks with Podemos, which remains neutral, while Zema’s allies expect his nomination to be approved unanimously at the convention.

item.title: Brasil colhe o que Lula plantou com tarifa dos EUA, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, pré-presidential candidate from Novo, blamed the Lula government for the new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, claiming foreign policy provoked tensions with Washington through rapprochement with Venezuela, Cuba, and Iran. He stated Brazil 'reaped what it sowed,' arguing the burden falls on productive sectors and taxpayers, not the political elite. The tariff takes effect July 22, 2026, impacting agribusiness and manufacturing, while the Brazilian government rejected the U.S. justification and pledged to challenge it at the WTO and invoke the Reciprocity Law.

item.title: Zema ironiza palanque do PT em MG: 'Patrus aceitou para ter sossego'
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais, mocked the PT's difficulty in building a political platform in the state, suggesting that deputy Patrus Ananias (PT) agreed to run for governor merely to 'have a little peace'.
